complexity.correctness_reason: A left- or right-skewed tree with more than roughly 1000 nodes (impossible under NeetCode's 100-node cap, but permitted once it is lifted) exceeds CPython's default recursion limit and raises RecursionError.
complexity.notes: Correct and readable. Stylistically, `not p and not q` is more idiomatic than `not (p or q)`, and comparing `p.val == q.val` before recursing would let unequal trees short-circuit slightly earlier. Space is O(h) recursion depth — O(log n) on balanced trees but O(n) on skewed ones, and because it recurses, a skewed tree deep enough to exceed Python's recursion limit would raise RecursionError; ||an iterative traversal with an explicit stack|| avoids that.
complexity.summary: Recursive simultaneous traversal of both trees: equal if both are None, unequal if exactly one is None, otherwise recurse on both children and compare values.
